title: PCXR-Copilot: Device-aware pediatric chest radiographic analysis with segmentation, suppression, and edema-related cues
abstract: Patients admitted to pediatric ICU and cardiac ICU often require intensive perioperative support and frequent chest radiography to monitor support devices, extravascular lung water, and body-wall edema. Radiographic interpretation and analysis is often difficult due to superimposed anatomic and iatrogenic structures that obscure clinically relevant signals. While deep learning can provide decision support, translation to pediatric radiographs is still limited by high device burden and scarcity of pediatric datasets with clinically grounded device annotations. To address this gap, we first introduce PediaDeviceSeg-1K, a curated dataset of 1,000 anterior-posterior radiographs of pediatric CICU patients with clinically grounded, fine-grained annotations of common ICU devices. To our best knowledge, this is the first publicly available pediatric CICU CXR resource with clinically grounded device annotations for device-focused benchmarking. Building on PediaDeviceSeg-1K, we further present PCXR-Copilot, a device-aware pipeline that outputs lung and device masks, optional device-suppressed views, and edema-related visualization maps and scalar indices. The full pipeline has been integrated and runs in real time within the TWIST platform at Boston Children's Hospital, demonstrating feasibility for real-world clinical deployment.

title: SlimFormer++: Token Mixing Where It Matters for Efficient 3D Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: To determine where computation is needed in volumetric segmentation networks, we analyze block-level redundancy and stage-wise token-mixer contribution. Centered Kernel Alignment reveals high input-output representational similarity within blocks of representative convolutional, hybrid, and Transformer-style segmentation networks. Similarity-guided pruning reduces their parameter counts by 39-75% while decreasing mean Dice by less than 0.4 percentage points. To examine token mixers within blocks, we introduce Anatomical Relation Distortion, which quantifies how bypassing a mixer distorts feature relations between labeled anatomical positions. Applied to an unpruned candidate architecture, Centered Kernel Alignment indicates high representational redundancy in intermediate encoder mixers, whereas Anatomical Relation Distortion shows that they contribute little and the bottleneck mixer most. These findings motivate SlimFormer++, which uses Selective Mixing blocks with windowed Mamba mixing in the first encoder stage and only residual channel MLPs in deeper stages. At the bottleneck, Augmented Mixing injects similarity-weighted sparse long-range context into the axial taps of a depthwise convolution at cost linear in voxel count. Evaluated against 12 baselines across eight public CT, MRI, and ultrasound datasets (1,809 cases), SlimFormer++ achieves the highest mean Dice (87.84%) and lowest mean HD95 (6.50 mm) with the fewest parameters (5.98 million). These results support stage-aware token mixing as a design strategy for improving the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in volumetric segmentation. The source code is available at https://github.com/WHHHHHY822/SlimFormerPlusPlus

title: Deep Auxiliary Learning via Bilevel Feature Optimization for Label-Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
abstract: Auxiliary learning (AL), which can improve the performance of a primary task by leveraging related auxiliary tasks, is commonly regarded as a special case of multi-task learning. Existing AL approaches typically require manually annotated auxiliary labels, increasing annotation costs, particularly in medical imaging where expert labeling is expensive. In this work, we investigate whether segmentation performance can be improved using auxiliary tasks whose labels are automatically derived from existing segmentation annotations, requiring no additional manual labeling. To address this, we propose a novel auxiliary learning framework, formulated as a bilevel optimization problem. Our method enables effective knowledge transfer between tasks via a feature communication module, enhancing the primary segmentation task. We evaluate the method on three medical image segmentation benchmarks under limited-label settings. The results demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior label efficiency. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/FupingWu90/ALBO.

title: Foundation Model-Enabled Pathology-Informed MRI Model for Preoperative Prediction of Vessels Encapsulating Tumor Clusters in Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model-enabled framework for pathology-informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI. PIVOT-MRI uses morphologic and vascular embedding alignment, and PIVOT-Clinical combines the PIVOT-MRI score with tumor size and alpha-fetoprotein. The multicenter retrospective study includes 2052 patients in a training cohort, an internal test cohort, and four external validation cohorts. PIVOT-MRI achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.887 in the internal test cohort and 0.839-0.861 across external cohorts. PIVOT-Clinical increases the internal-test area under the curve to 0.904 and PIVOT-Clinical-defined groups are associated with different two-year recurrence risks. Removing both histopathologic alignment branches results in the largest ablation-related performance decrease. Exploratory radiotranscriptomic analyses showed that higher PIVOT-MRI scores were associated with angiogenesis-related, endothelial, and proliferative transcriptional programs. PIVOT enables noninvasive preoperative assessment of pathology-defined vascular aggressiveness in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma while preserving an MRI-only clinical inference pathway.

title: Trans-Patch Retrograde Re-Entry During Hybrid Revascularization of an External Iliac Artery Chronic Total Occlusion: A Technical Note and Review of Re-Entry Strategies.
abstract: Failure of true-lumen re-entry after subintimal wire passage is a well-recognized limitation of endovascular treatment for external iliac artery (EIA) chronic total occlusions (CTO). We report a 73-year-old woman with severe limb ischemia and a prior failed endovascular attempt who underwent hybrid left common femoral artery (CFA) endarterectomy with patch angioplasty, followed by trans-patch retrograde access and dedicated device-assisted re-entry (Outback Elite) after antegrade and retrograde wires repeatedly tracked subintimally without reaching the true lumen. Controlled re-entry preserved hypogastric artery flow and allowed drug-eluting stent reconstruction of the EIA. At 12-month follow-up, ABI improved from 0.36 to 0.50, and TBI improved to 0.37. Duplex ultrasound at 6-month follow-up confirmed patency of the reconstructed segment without evidence of hemodynamically significant restenosis. This technical report illustrates the use of an endarterectomized CFA as a retrograde re-entry platform and reviews contemporary strategies for managing subintimal crossing failure in iliac CTOs.

title: Advancing Early Breast Cancer Diagnosis and Ki-67 Expression Prediction With Ultrasound Viscoelastography: Based on Peritumoral Assessment.
abstract: Background Breast cancer is the most common invasive malignancy in women. Ultrasound viscoelastography may improve non-invasive diagnosis, but the clinical relevance of peritumoral viscoelastic parameters (VPs) and their correlation with Ki-67 remain unclear. This study explores these associations. Methods A prospective study enrolled 256 breast masses (156 malignant, 100 benign). Patients underwent conventional ultrasound and viscoelastography. VPs were acquired within masses (A), peritumoral shells (Shell1: 1 mm, Shell2: 2 mm, Shell3: 3 mm), and combined regions (A' = A + Shell). Quantitative metrics included elasticity (V/1 E, V/0 E), dispersion coefficient (V/1 D), viscosity coefficient (V/0 V), and their maximum (Max), minimum (Min), mean(Mean), and standard deviation (SD) values. Diagnostic performance was evaluated by analyzing the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and calculating the area under the curve (AUC), followed by logistic regression. VPs were compared between high/low Ki-67 groups. Results The AUCs of peritumoral VPs exceeded those from masses. V/1 D showed higher AUC than V/0 V and elasticity values, with Shell3 V/1 D SD having the highest AUC (0.840). The diagnostic efficacy of the peritumoral viscoelastic model surpassed that of the single elasticity parameter model, with 89.1% sensitivity, 73% specificity, 82.8% accuracy. Key variables included Shell3 V/1 D and Shell3 V/0 E. Shell1 V/0 V Max was significantly higher in high versus low Ki-67 expression groups ( p < 0.05). title: Histopathological Spectrum in FIT-Positive Patients With Abnormal Colonoscopy Findings at a Tertiary Medical Center in Lebanon: A Retrospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background and aims Colorectal cancer is a leading cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality, and the prognosis significantly depends on the diagnostic stage. Various screening initiatives have been established, among which the fecal immunochemical test (FIT) (FITFIT) which is prominent for its affordability, non-invasive approach, and wide acceptance. This study aimed to describe the spectrum of histopathological findings among patients with positive fecal occult blood test and abnormal colonoscopy findings, and to identify associated risk factors. Methods This retrospective observational study included 172 adults with documented positive FIT and abnormal colonoscopy findings at Makassed General Hospital from January 2024 to December 2025. Statistical analysis was conducted using SPSS version 25, and associations were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests, with significance defined as p < 0.05. Results A total of 172 patients were included, with a mean age of 63.88 ± 11.79 years, and 55.2% were female. The most frequently recorded indications for colonoscopy were anemia (39%) and screening (37.2%). Polyps were the most common colonoscopy finding. Histopathological examination demonstrated that neoplastic polyps represented the predominant diagnosis (65.1%), followed by non-neoplastic lesions (24.4%) and malignancy (10.5%). Patients aged 45 years and older demonstrated a higher prevalence of polyps on colonoscopy; however, the difference did not reach statistical significance. No significant association was observed between gender and colonoscopy or histopathological findings. Abdominal pain and diarrhea were both significantly associated with non-neoplastic histopathological lesions. Conclusion Among patients with positive FIT and abnormal colonoscopy findings, neoplastic polyps rather than malignancy represented the predominant histopathological findings, supporting the clinical utility of FIT in detecting clinically important colorectal lesions at earlier stages. In addition, variability in the histopathology depending on the clinical presentation may contribute to clinical assessment and risk stratification. Larger prospective studies are needed to determine predictors of advanced colorectal histopathology.

title: Defining the Clinical Indication for Real-Time Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ultrasound in Breast Lesions with Low Suspicion of Malignancy.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate whether real-time artificial intelligence (AI) breast ultrasound (US) can identify a subgroup of breast imaging reporting and data system (BI-RADS) category 4A lesions without suspicious mammographic (MMG) findings in whom unnecessary biopsy may be safely avoided. Methods This retrospective analysis of single-center biopsy registry included 641 consecutive US BI-RADS 4A lesions that underwent vacuum-assisted breast biopsy. Before conducting biopsy, the lesions were reassessed using a real-time AI US system (CadAI-B®), and MMG findings were classified as suspicious or non-suspicious based on formal reports. Seven prespecified biopsy-decision strategies were evaluated, including 3 AI-only strategies, 3 mammography-gated AI strategies, and the current standard strategy of biopsy all BI-RADS 4A lesions. The primary outcomes were biopsy reduction rate, missed cancers, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, and accuracy, with final pathology as the reference standard. Results Among 641 cases of US BI-RADS 4A lesions, 26 cases of malignancies (4.1%) were identified, including 14 cases of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS), 11 cases of invasive ductal carcinomas, and 1 case of apocrine carcinoma. AI reassigned 289 cases of lesions (45.1%) to BI-RADS categories 1-3. AI-only biopsy-deferral strategies missed 30.8% and 38.5% of malignancies when biopsy was deferred for AI BI-RADS ≤2 and ≤3 lesions, respectively, with DCIS accounting for most missed cancers. In contrast, among lesions without suspicious MMG findings, no malignancies were observed in AI BI-RADS 1-3 lesions. The sequential strategy of deferring biopsy only for lesions with AI BI-RADS ≤3 and non-suspicious MMG findings reduced biopsies by 43.5% (279/641) while maintaining 100.0% sensitivity (95% CI, 87.1-100.0%) and increasing specificity to 45.4% (95% CI, 41.4-49.4%). Conclusion Real-time AI breast US alone could not safely support biopsy deferral in US BI-RADS 4A lesions. However, after suspicious MMG findings had been excluded, AI identified a low-risk subgroup in whom unnecessary biopsy could be substantially reduced without compromising cancer detection. These findings suggest that the clinical utility of real-time AI breast US lies in patients without suspicious MMG findings. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Asymptomatic Portomesenteric Venous Thrombosis After Colorectal Cancer Surgery: Incidence, Natural History, and Implications for Management.
abstract: Background Portomesenteric venous thrombosis (PMVT) after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery is most often reported in symptomatic patients, leaving its frequency and natural history across the asymptomatic spectrum poorly defined. When encountered incidentally, it frequently prompts anticoagulation, hypercoagulability evaluation, or delays in oncologic treatment, despite limited evidence that intervention alters its course. Using a cohort with routine postoperative imaging, we characterized the incidence, anatomic distribution, risk factors, and clinical course of asymptomatic PMVT. Methods We retrospectively studied 799 consecutive patients who underwent CRC surgery between April 2019 and June 2025. All patients underwent standardized abdominal computed tomography (CT) on postoperative day (POD) 6 as part of our institutional clinical pathway for immediate postoperative follow-up. PMVT was defined radiologically, and thrombus location was classified as peripheral intrahepatic branches or main portal/superior mesenteric vein. Management followed a risk-stratified pathway of therapeutic anticoagulation or active surveillance, with radiologic resolution assessed on follow-up CT. Given the limited number of events, multivariable analysis was considered exploratory. Results Asymptomatic PMVT was identified in 33 patients (4.1%), none symptomatic at detection. Thrombi were predominantly confined to the distal intrahepatic branches. In exploratory multivariable analysis, age ≤ 60 years (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.19-5.03, p = 0.015) and POD 5 WBC > 10 × 10 9 /L (OR 2.39, 95% CI 1.16-4.93, p = 0.018) were independently associated with PMVT. Twenty-one patients received anticoagulation and 12 were managed with surveillance alone. Complete radiologic resolution occurred in all 33 patients within one year, including every patient managed without anticoagulation. Furthermore, there were no cases of thrombus extension, portal hypertension, or bowel ischemia. Conclusion When postoperative imaging is routinely performed, asymptomatic PMVT after CRC surgery is detected in approximately 4% of patients. It is typically confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and follows a uniformly benign self-limiting course, even in patients managed without anticoagulation. These findings argue against reflexive anticoagulation and extensive workup for short-segment, non-occlusive PMVT confined to peripheral intrahepatic branches, and support an individualized, predominantly conservative approach. We do not advocate routine postoperative CT; rather, surgeons who encounter incidental PMVT can be reassured regarding its favorable prognosis.

title: Awareness, need and utilization of breast cancer risk management resources in women with hereditary cancer susceptibility.
abstract: Background Germline genetic testing is increasing. While testing barriers are well characterized, less is known about post-testing needs and utilization of screening and prevention resources by women with pathogenic variants (PVs) in breast cancer susceptibility genes. Methods A 38-question online survey was developed by Facing Our Risk of Cancer Empowered (FORCE), a patient advocacy group, and administered electronically to subscribers from February-May 2024. Study eligibility criteria included female sex and a germline PV conferring elevated lifetime risk of breast cancer (ATM, BARD1, BRCA1, BRCA2, CDH1, CHEK2, PALB2, PTEN, RAD51C, RAD51D, STK11, or TP53). Results Of 1,025 respondents who initiated the survey, 937 were women. Most were non-Hispanic White (91.7%) and from the United States (81.6%). The most common PVs were BRCA2 (31.4%), BRCA1 (25.5%) and CHEK2 (9.2%). The most frequently used resources were education and information services about medical options (39.3%) and peer support (28.1%). Few respondents used financial navigation (4.0%) or financial support (5.3%), but up to 45% reported needing these services. Among breast screening users (53.8% used mammogram, 42.2% magnetic resonance imaging, 19.4% ultrasound), 37.8% found it hard to prepare emotionally for results and 14% found it hard to pay for screening. One-third (37.1%) of respondents found deciding whether to have risk-reducing mastectomy hard; two-thirds (64.0%) found physical recovery hard, more than half (60.2%) found emotional recovery hard, and one-quarter (24.7%) found paying for risk-reducing mastectomy hard. Conclusion In this contemporary sample of women at elevated risk of breast cancer, more than one-third had unmet financial needs and up to two-thirds had difficulty with screening or risk-reducing surgery. Closing these gaps will be essential to improve outcomes for women with hereditary breast cancer.

title: Morphometric analysis and three-dimensional reconstruction of sphenoid sinus: Associations of linear dimensions and volume with pneumatization patterns and neurovascular relationships.
abstract: Background The sphenoid sinus (SS) shows morphological variability relevant to endoscopic endonasal skull-base access. This study examined associations of SS volume and linear dimensions with pneumatization patterns, extensions, and neurovascular anatomy. Methods This retrospective study included 253 adult sinus computed tomography (CT) examinations. Μaximum anteroposterior (AP max), laterolateral (LL max), and craniocaudal (CC max) dimensions were measured, and SS volume was calculated by semi-automated three-dimensional contouring with manual refinement. Pneumatization patterns and relationships with the internal carotid artery (ICA), optic nerve (ON), and Vidian nerve (VN) were examined using exploratory univariable logistic regression, supplemented by separate age- and sex-adjusted models for neurovascular outcomes. Results Mean SS volume was 11.12 ± 4.50 cm³. Males had greater volume (p = 0.001) and AP max (p = 0.013) than females. Volume correlated strongly with LL max (r = 0.791) and AP max (r = 0.705) (both p < 0.001). Each 1-mm increase in AP max was associated with posterior extension (OR = 1.57, 95% CI 1.40-1.76) and ICA (OR = 1.22), ON (OR = 1.13), and VN (OR = 1.24) protrusion and/or dehiscence. Each 1-mm increase in LL max was associated with lateral extension (OR = 1.39, 95% CI 1.28-1.52) and VN protrusion and/or dehiscence (OR = 1.24, 95% CI 1.18-1.31) (p < 0.001). Greater SS volume was associated with protrusion and/or dehiscence of all three structures, and remained associated with these neurovascular outcomes after adjustment for age and sex. Conclusions SS volume and linear dimensions provide complementary quantitative information on the magnitude and direction of pneumatization. AP max and LL max were associated with specific extension patterns and with neurovascular protrusion and/or dehiscence.

title: Clinical phenotype and bone microarchitecture of cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome: experience from a single center in China.
abstract: Context Cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome (CSHS) is a rare mosaic RASopathy characterized by epidermal or melanocytic nevi, skeletal dysplasia, and fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)-mediated hypophosphatemic rickets. However, its bone microarchitectural features remain underdefined. Objectives The study aimed to characterize the clinical, genetic, and skeletal microarchitectural features of CSHS. Methods We summarized clinical findings of 6 CSHS patients with genetically confirmed somatic RAS mutations. Skeletal involvement was assessed by whole-body bone scintigraphy. High-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography parameters at the distal radius and tibia were compared with age- and sex-matched XLH controls (1:3). Literature review of 24 genetically confirmed CSHS patients was performed to assess genotype-phenotype correlation. Results All patients were confirmed to carry somatic HRAS or NRAS mutation in affected skin. Hypophosphatemia, elevated alkaline phosphatase and elevated FGF23 were found in all patients. Genotype-phenotype correlation analysis did not identify any significant biochemical or systemic burden differences across 3 genotypes. Compared with XLH controls, CSHS patients exhibited significantly reduced total and trabecular volumetric BMD (vBMD), with relatively preserved cortical vBMD. Bone cross-sectional geometry was less expanded than in XLH at the tibia. In addition, thinner trabeculae with greater separation were found at the radius, and the distal tibia showed thinner cortices and decreased cortical porosity. Estimated bone stiffness and failure load were significantly lower at both the radius and tibia. Conclusions CSHS is associated with pronounced trabecular vBMD impairment and reduced bone strength compared with XLH controls. These findings are consistent with a combined contribution of intrinsic skeletal dysplasia and chronic hypophosphatemia on bone, although further studies are needed to elucidate these mechanisms.

title: Preliminary study on early microvascular ingrowth into distracted callus during distraction osteogenesis-A non-invasive approach to explore the early growth patterns and possible mechanism of distraction osteogenesis in vivo.
abstract: Background Distraction osteogenesis (DO) is critical for repairing large segmental bone defects. Early callus vascularization is essential for bone regeneration; however, real-time microcirculatory assessment remains lacking. This study aimed to elucidate spatiotemporal microvascular network construction in distracted callus using super-resolution contrast-enhanced ultrasound (SR CEUS) and high-frame-rate contrast-enhanced ultrasound (HiFR CEUS) in a sheep tibial DO model. Methods Six sheep underwent tibial DO. On day 7 of distraction, B-mode ultrasound, "Firefly" imaging, SR CEUS, and HiFR CEUS were performed. Quantitative parameters including vessel density (VD), perfusion index (PI), mean intensity, and peak intensity (PKI) were compared among three regions: central high-perfusion area (CHPA), annular low-perfusion area (ALPA), and peripheral high-perfusion area (PHPA). Results B-mode ultrasound revealed outward bulging of distracted callus. "Firefly" imaging detected microcalcifications. SR CEUS showed PHPA (67.58% of cross-sectional area) received centripetal blood flow from periosteum and surrounding soft tissues; CHPA (10.39%) received centrifugal flow from the medullary cavity; ALPA (22.03%), located between them, exhibited significantly lower mean intensity than CHPA/PHPA and significantly lower VD and PI than PHPA (P < 0.05). HiFR CEUS showed perfusion appeared first in CHPA, then PHPA, and lastly ALPA. Conclusion SR and HiFR CEUS enable non-invasive, dynamic visualization and quantification of microvascular growth in distracted callus, revealing a "target ring sign", "bidirectional fusion" perfusion pattern, and "central-first, peripheral-second" perfusion sequence. ALPA was identified as a hypovascular zone potentially associated with delayed mineralization or cyst formation. This system provides a novel imaging framework for early assessment of callus viability, prediction of osteogenic risk, and guidance of individualized distraction strategies.

title: Multi-center study of CMR versus cardiac catheterization with endomyocardial biopsy for pediatric transplant surveillance: study protocol.
abstract: Notwithstanding advances in post-transplant care, acute allograft rejection (AR) remains the leading cause of mortality in pediatric heart transplant recipients (PHTX). Endomyocardial biopsy (EMB) continues to be the standard of care for AR detection, despite being invasive, costly, and associated with patient discomfort and potential complications. Non-invasive alternatives, including cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) with T1 and T2 parametric mapping and blood biomarkers (BB) such as cell-free DNA (cfDNA) and microRNA (miRNA), have shown promise in the adult transplant population, but their validation in the pediatric transplant population is lacking. The "Predictive Modeling of Acute Rejection in Pediatric Heart Transplant Recipients" (PEACE) study is a prospective, multicenter trial aiming to assess the diagnostic accuracy of CMR and BB in comparison to EMB. The goal of this manuscript is to describe the purpose and experimental protocol of the PEACE study. The PEACE study's overarching hypothesis is that CMR and BB can consistently and accurately detect myocardial abnormalities, potentially guiding the need for EMB. Secondary objectives include cost-analyses of CMR and BB, as well as a biomarker performance evaluation in biopsy-negative, but symptomatic and suspected AR cases. PEACE will enroll PHTX ages 6-25 years, across approximately 20 U.S. pediatric hospitals. All subjects will undergo EMB for surveillance or suspected AR as standard of care. As part of the research protocol, subjects will undergo blood collection for BB prior to the EMB and CMR within 5 days of EMB. Central core labs will conduct blinded analysis for imaging, pathology, and biomarkers to ensure consistent data interpretation. PEACE represents a critical step in reducing reliance on invasive biopsies in the clinical care of PHTX. By validating non-invasive tools in a large, diverse population, the PEACE study could transform AR detection, resulting in improvement of the patient experience and outcomes in this vulnerable population. (Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT07770659, Non-invasive Prediction of EArly Cardiac rEjection (PEACE)).

title: Adaptive local region super-resolution for high-field MRI: A diffusion-based approach with structural and frequency-domain constraints.
abstract: High-field MRI offers superior SNR but is constrained by the trade-off between spatial resolution and acquisition time. Existing global deep learning super-resolution (SR) methods often incur computational overhead by ignoring regional image content. This motivates an adaptive local SR strategy to optimize efficiency and detail preservation. To address this, we developed a local SR method that adaptively allocates computational resources to information-rich regions. The proposed framework regularized an entropy-based local region processing strategy with a diffusion model fortified by frequency-domain and structural constraints. We retrospectively evaluated our method on two diverse datasets: a proprietary 7.0 T dental MRI dataset (25 T2-weighted DESS sequences from 10 beagle dogs) and a public 5.0 T brain MRI dataset (Diff5T, 50 diffusion-weighted sequences). Image quality was quantified using PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID. On the 7.0 T dental test dataset (2 subjects), our method achieved a PSNR of 27.31 [26.83, 27.79] dB and the lowest LPIPS of 0.19 [0.18, 0.20]. On the 5.0 T brain test dataset (10 subjects), the method achieved a PSNR of 27.15 ± 0.10 dB, an LPIPS of 0.14 ± 0.00 and an FID of 54.01, with lower perceptual metrics than the evaluated baselines. Ablation studies indicated that the proposed frequency-domain and structural constraints reduced LPIPS and FID, with trade-offs in PSNR and SSIM. In conclusion, the evaluated framework showed improvements in perceptual metrics by integrating targeted local processing with frequency-domain and structural regularization, accompanied by a trade-off in pixel-wise fidelity metrics, supporting the technical feasibility of addressing the resolution-time trade-off in high-field MRI. Future work will focus on expanding the dataset and evaluating the framework in human dental cohorts to address anatomical differences between the current canine model and human dental anatomy.

title: CAG repeat length shapes bidirectional functional connectome alterations in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3: a multimodal MRI study.
abstract: The ATXN3 gene is the primary driver of brain damage in spinocerebellar ataxia type 3 (SCA3). We aimed to elucidate the patterns of connectome alterations shaped by cytosine-adenine-guanine (CAG) repeat length in SCA3. Eighty-nine genetically confirmed patients with SCA3 and 89 age-, sex-, education-matched healthy controls underwent multimodal MRI and comprehensive clinical assessments. Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) was used to identify functional connectivity patterns associated with CAG repeat length. Structural brain damage was assessed using voxel-based morphometry. Mediation analysis was performed to examine the role of structural impairment in connectivity changes. CPM identified a positive and a negative network, whose connectivity strength increased or decreased with CAG repeat length. The positive network (r = 0.397, P < 0.001) was mainly localized within the cerebello-motor circuit and was positively associated with ataxia severity and functional disability. The negative network (r = 0.243, P = 0.022) was distributed across large-scale networks, with selective vulnerability of interhemispheric connectivity, and was associated with motor dysfunction. Besides the canonical motor pathways, limbic-related connectivity was related to motor impairment. Structural analyses revealed widespread gray matter atrophy centered on the cerebellum. Cerebellar atrophy statistically mediated the association between CAG repeat length and connectivity decreases. CAG repeat length is associated with a bidirectional connectopathy in SCA3. Cerebellar atrophy may mediate the connectivity decreases. Future longitudinal studies are required to examine the underlying causal pathway.

title: The PENIMA project: artificial intelligence decision-support tool for penile lesions - protocol paper and invitation to participate.
abstract: Objectives To present and describe the design, data collection framework, and interim cohort characteristics of the PENIMA project, a multicentre initiative establishing a clinically annotated penile lesion image repository to support future artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision-support development - and to encourage urology and dermatology colleagues working with penile lesions to participate in the project. Patients and methods Prospective participant inclusion commenced in March 2023 across Scandinavian urological and dermatological departments. Patients with penile anatomy undergoing clinically indicated genital examination are invited to participate and provide oral and written consent as defined by local authority regulations. Clinical photographs and structured metadata are collected. Lesion classification is based on a specialist evaluation, clinical follow-up and histopathology when available. Images are pseudonymised and annotated using a secure, containerised Computer Vision Annotation Tool (CVAT) environment. Supervised machine-learning model development using convolutional neural networks is planned with patient-level dataset partitioning and evaluation using standard diagnostic performance metrics. The study was approved by relevant local authorities, and the approval number is 1-10-72-150-22. Results As of February 2026, 1125 participants and approximately 7000 images have been included. In all, 40% represented normal anatomical variants. Among lesional cases, 33% are clinically assessed as benign, 13% premalignant, and 8% malignant; 22% of all cases have histopathological verification. Concordance between clinical suspicion and histopathology is highest for penile carcinoma (84.6%, 95% confidence interval 75.0-91.0%). Conclusion The PENIMA project includes a multicentre, clinically grounded image repository reflecting real-world penile lesion presentations. The feasible and successful infrastructure provides a foundation for future development and validation of image-based clinical decision-support tools.

title: Segment-based comparison of multiparametric MRI, Gallium-68-PSMA-PET/CT and combined imaging with histopathology in prostate cancer.
abstract: Objectives To compare the segment-based diagnostic performance of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), Gallium-68-prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography/computed tomography ( 68 Ga-PSMA-PET/CT), for detecting histopathologically confirmed prostate cancer (PCa). Patients and methods This analysis included 97 men from the prospective, interventional, phase II DEPROMP (DEtection rate of clinically significant PROstate cancer by mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT fusion biopsy) trial who underwent radical prostatectomy with whole-mount histopathological evaluation. All participants received mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT prior to biopsy. The mpMRI was interpreted according to Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version(v)2.1, and PSMA-PET/CT according to Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardised Evaluation (PROMISE) molecular imaging Tumour-Node-Metastasis (miTNM) criteria. The prostate was divided into 36 anatomical segments based on the PI-RADS v2.1 sector map. Each segment was correlated with histopathological findings from prostatectomy specimens. For each imaging modality, detection rates, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated at the segment level. Results A total of 3492 prostate segments were analysed. Detection rates were 74.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 72.6-75.5) for mpMRI, 72.2% (95% CI 70.6-73.6) for PSMA-PET/CT, and 79.1% (95% CI 77.7-80.4) for the combined use of mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT. Sensitivity and specificity were 13.4% and 97.3% for mpMRI, 18.5% and 92.7% for PSMA-PET/CT, and 25.8% and 90.5% for combined mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT, respectively. Threshold-based receiver operating characteristic analyses yielded an AUC of 0.62 (95% CI 0.54-0.69) for PI-RADS, 0.68 (95% CI 0.63-0.74) for maximum standardised uptake value, and 0.69 (95% CI 0.65-0.74) for molecular imaging PSMA. Conclusion At the segment level, mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT showed comparable diagnostic accuracy with high specificity but limited sensitivity. Their combination improved sensitivity and overall detection performance, underscoring the complementary value of structural and molecular imaging for lesion localisation and precision management in PCa.

To compare the segment-based diagnostic performance of multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI), Gallium-68-prostate-specific membrane antigen-positron emission tomography/computed tomography (68Ga-PSMA-PET/CT), for detecting histopathologically confirmed prostate cancer (PCa).

Patients and methods

This analysis included 97 men from the prospective, interventional, phase II DEPROMP (DEtection rate of clinically significant PROstate cancer by mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT fusion biopsy) trial who underwent radical prostatectomy with whole-mount histopathological evaluation. All participants received mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT prior to biopsy. The mpMRI was interpreted according to Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) version(v)2.1, and PSMA-PET/CT according to Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardised Evaluation (PROMISE) molecular imaging Tumour-Node-Metastasis (miTNM) criteria. The prostate was divided into 36 anatomical segments based on the PI-RADS v2.1 sector map. Each segment was correlated with histopathological findings from prostatectomy specimens. For each imaging modality, detection rates, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) were calculated at the segment level.

Results

A total of 3492 prostate segments were analysed. Detection rates were 74.1% (95% confidence interval [CI] 72.6-75.5) for mpMRI, 72.2% (95% CI 70.6-73.6) for PSMA-PET/CT, and 79.1% (95% CI 77.7-80.4) for the combined use of mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT. Sensitivity and specificity were 13.4% and 97.3% for mpMRI, 18.5% and 92.7% for PSMA-PET/CT, and 25.8% and 90.5% for combined mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT, respectively. Threshold-based receiver operating characteristic analyses yielded an AUC of 0.62 (95% CI 0.54-0.69) for PI-RADS, 0.68 (95% CI 0.63-0.74) for maximum standardised uptake value, and 0.69 (95% CI 0.65-0.74) for molecular imaging PSMA.

Conclusion

At the segment level, mpMRI and PSMA-PET/CT showed comparable diagnostic accuracy with high specificity but limited sensitivity. Their combination improved sensitivity and overall detection performance, underscoring the complementary value of structural and molecular imaging for lesion localisation and precision management in PCa.

title: Transient apnoea for motion control during flexible ureteroscopic lithotripsy: a randomised trial.
abstract: Objectives To determine whether transient apnoea (TA) during flexible ureteroscopic laser lithotripsy improves active lithotripsy efficiency compared with regular mechanical ventilation (RMV) and small tidal-volume ventilation (STVV). Patients and methods In this single-centre, three-arm randomised trial, 150 adults with a single computed tomography (CT)-confirmed renal, ureteropelvic, or proximal ureteric stone measuring 10-<20 mm were assigned one-to-one-to-one to RMV, STVV, or TA. TA followed 5-min 100% oxygen pre-oxygenation, with 9-min maximum and pre-specified stopping criteria under continuous anaesthetic monitoring. The primary endpoint was active lithotripsy efficiency, defined as CT-estimated stone volume divided by elapsed active lithotripsy time. Analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle. Results The mean (standard deviation) active lithotripsy efficiency was 27.8 (8.9), 26.6 (8.0), and 34.3 (10.0) mm 3 /min with RMV, STVV, and TA, respectively (P < 0.001). TA increased adjusted efficiency by 5.9 mm 3 /min vs RMV (95% confidence interval [CI] 2.2-9.6 mm 3 /min) and 6.8 mm 3 /min vs STVV (95% CI 3.3-10.2 mm 3 /min). The median active lithotripsy time was 27.5, 26.5, and 22.0 min (P = 0.001); total operative time was 50.0, 50.0, and 43.0 min (P = 0.002); and surgeon-rated targeting stability scores were 7.0, 7.0, and 9.0 (P < 0.001), respectively. Postoperative Day 1/1-month stone-free rates were 88%/92%, 80%/96%, and 88%/90%, respectively, with no significant between-group differences. The median (interquartile range) achieved apnoea duration was 5.0 (4.5-6.8) min; 46/50 resumed ventilation before the 9-min maximum, most commonly for heart-rate decline/bradycardia (n = 27) or blood-pressure decline/hypotension (n = 20). No patient had a peripheral oxygen saturation <90% or a Clavien-Dindo Grade ≥III complication; transient hypercapnia and respiratory acidosis improved after ventilation resumed. Conclusion Transient apnoea improved lithotripsy efficiency and shortened operative time compared with RMV and STVV, with higher surgeon-rated targeting stability. The benefit was primarily intraoperative, without evidence of greater postoperative stone clearance. Protocolised TA may provide a brief intraoperative motion-control option with pre-oxygenation, continuous anaesthetic monitoring, and individualised termination.

title: A Familial Case of Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre Syndrome (TROFAS), Presenting With Postaxial Polydactyly and Upper Lip Vascular Malformation.
abstract: Thauvin-Robinet-Faivre syndrome (TROFAS, OMIM #617107) is a recently identified autosomal recessive disorder characterised by syndromic overgrowth, facial dysmorphism, mild intellectual disability, variable congenital anomalies, and occasional tumour occurrence. TROFAS results from homozygous or compound heterozygous variants in the FIBP gene, encoding the intracellular binding protein for acidic fibroblast growth factor. This protein plays a role in the fibroblast growth factor (FGF) signalling pathway, which is involved in cell proliferation and contributes to the development of several structures, such as the nervous system, optic vesicles, and blood vessels. Prior to the present report, TROFAS has been described in 10 patients from seven families, four of which are of Turkish origin. We report two additional Turkish siblings from a previously unreported family harbouring the recurrent homozygous c.412-3_415dupCAGTTTG likely pathogenic variant in FIBP. Both presented with typical TROFAS features; however, the male sibling exhibited a more severe neurodevelopmental profile and additional malformations, including postaxial polydactyly and upper lip vascular malformation, which, to our knowledge, have not previously been reported in association with TROFAS. A detailed clinical characterisation of these two new cases contributes to a more comprehensive delineation of the syndrome, adding potentially novel phenotypic features requiring confirmation in additional patients.

title: PRAME Immunohistochemistry and Molecular Profiling in Undifferentiated Cutaneous Pleomorphic Neoplasms: A Case Series of 8 Tumors.
abstract: Background Undifferentiated cutaneous pleomorphic neoplasms are diagnostically challenging, as histopathology and immunohistochemistry often fail to identify undifferentiated melanoma in lesions that instead remain classified provisionally as atypical fibroxanthoma (AFX) or pleomorphic dermal sarcoma (PDS). Given the prognostic and therapeutic implications of melanoma, additional ancillary tools may be helpful in selected cases. Methods We studied eight patients with undifferentiated pleomorphic neoplasms using molecular profiling and PRAME immunohistochemistry, correlating findings with clinical behavior. Results Molecular findings varied across the cohort. Two tumors harbored NRAS hotspot mutations and were associated with aggressive clinical courses. In one patient, the tumor showed focal melanoma in situ associated with an undifferentiated intradermal tumor harboring NF1, TERT, and TP53 variants. The remaining tumors lacked melanoma-associated hotspot mutations. Diffuse PRAME expression was seen in three patients with an established diagnosis of melanoma and three patients with AFX/PDS. Two patients with AFX/PDS were negative for PRAME expression. Conclusions Molecular profiling may provide supportive diagnostic evidence for melanoma lineage in a subset of undifferentiated cutaneous pleomorphic neoplasms when interpreted in conjunction with morphology, immunohistochemistry, and clinical findings. In contrast, diffuse PRAME expression was observed in a nonspecific fashion both in cases with melanoma driver mutations and molecularly nonspecific cases in this cohort, limiting its utility as a standalone screening test for triaging molecular analysis.

title: Ηip dysplasia in children with spina bifida after prenatal surgical closure.
abstract: Aim To determine the prevalence of neonatal hip dysplasia in children with spina bifida after prenatal surgical closure and examine its association with functional level and preterm birth. Method We conducted a retrospective analysis of prospectively collected standardized registry data from a tertiary specialized centre providing comprehensive spina bifida diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up. Standardized hip ultrasound according to the Graf method was performed as part of a protocolized clinical pathway after prenatal surgery, within the first week of life corrected for preterm birth. The primary outcome was the prevalence of hip dysplasia at the initial ultrasound. Associations between hip status, functional level, and gestational age were assessed using Spearman's rank correlation. Results A total of 212 children (101 males, 111 females) underwent prenatal surgical closure between 1st January 2011 and 30th August 2022; 168 children (336 hips) had available neonatal ultrasound data and were included in the analysis. Preterm birth was present in 138 (82%) of 168 children, including 99 (59%) born late preterm, 35 (21%) born very preterm, and four (2%) born extremely preterm. At the initial ultrasound, 286 (85%) of 336 hips were mature, 33 (9.8%) were immature, and 17 (5.1%) were dysplastic. Worse hip status was weakly associated with a higher functional level (r = -0.243; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was found between hip dysplasia and preterm birth (p = 0.080). Interpretation The prevalence of neonatal hip dysplasia in children with spina bifida after prenatal surgical closure was within the range reported for the general population.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Ultrasound for Sarcopenia Assessment: A Scoping Review.
abstract: Background Muscle ultrasound offers a portable, non-invasive, and cost-effective option for sarcopenia assessment, but operator dependency limits its standardization. Artificial intelligence (AI) may help automate and improve ultrasound-based muscle evaluation. This scoping review aims to map the current landscape of AI-assisted ultrasound for sarcopenia assessment, including research trends, methods, clinical uses and performance, and to suggest future work. Methods Following Joanna Briggs Institute guidelines and the PRISMA-ScR checklist, we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CINAHL, ProQuest, CNKI, WanFang Data, Yiigle, VIP, and Sinomed up to July 25, 2026. Two researchers independently selected studies and extracted data. Results Thirty studies were included. This field is developing rapidly, with 76.7% of studies published in the last 3 years, primarily from Spain and China. Model development and validation studies (43.3%) were most common. U-Net and its variants were the predominant AI architectures, mainly for image segmentation. B-mode ultrasound with high-frequency linear probes was frequently used. The rectus femoris was the most assessed muscle for sarcopenia (73.3%). AI-integrated models for sarcopenia diagnosis achieved AUCs of 0.640-0.950. Reported Dice coefficients for muscle segmentation ranged from 0.73 to 0.99. In-house datasets were used in 66.7% of the studies, and global classification labels were the most frequent annotation strategy (46.7%). Conclusions AI-assisted ultrasound shows potential for objective and scalable sarcopenia assessment but remains early-stage. Operator dependency in image acquisition has not been fully resolved. Further investigation should determine the added value of integrating multimodal imaging, combining diverse AI techniques, and evaluating multiple muscle groups. Future efforts should deepen image-processing strategies to extract clinically relevant features and facilitate standardized, scalable implementation in clinical practice.

title: Disseminated Tuberculosis With Ocular Involvement After 12 Years of Anti-TNF-α Therapy.
abstract: Background Ocular tuberculosis (TB) is an uncommon yet potentially vision-threatening manifestation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis , particularly difficult to diagnose in immunocompromised individuals. The increasing use of anti-tumor necrosis factor- α (anti-TNF- α ) agents has markedly heightened the risk of TB reactivation, often with disseminated or extrapulmonary involvement despite negative baseline screening. Case presentation We describe a 52-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis receiving long-term adalimumab and methotrexate who developed disseminated TB with pulmonary, splenic, and ocular involvement after 12 years of anti-TNF- α therapy. Baseline screening had shown a negative tuberculin skin test and an indeterminate interferon- γ release assay. She presented with constitutional and respiratory symptoms, whereas chest computed tomography demonstrated diffuse micronodular infiltrates consistent with miliary TB. Microbiological confirmation was obtained via bronchoalveolar lavage. Ophthalmologic evaluation revealed bilateral choroidal granulomas with subretinal edema, leading to a diagnosis of ocular TB. Standard antitubercular therapy (ATT) was initiated but required modification due to drug-induced liver injury. Adjunctive systemic corticosteroids were introduced after antimicrobial therapy and gradually tapered. The patient achieved progressive clinical, radiological, and ophthalmologic improvement, with gradual regression of choroidal lesions. Discussion This case underscores the persistent long-term risk of TB reactivation during prolonged anti-TNF- α therapy and highlights the limitations of current screening strategies in immunosuppressed patients. Ocular TB requires integration of systemic, clinical, and imaging findings; in this patient, microbiologically confirmed disseminated TB together with characteristic bilateral choroidal granulomas supported a definitive diagnosis. Management relies on prompt ATT, discontinuation of immunosuppression, and judicious use of adjunctive corticosteroids. Long-term follow-up is essential given the risk of persistent lesions and late recurrence. Reintroduction of biologic therapy may be feasible in selected cases but requires careful risk stratification. Conclusion TB should remain a diagnostic consideration in patients receiving biologic therapy who develop compatible systemic or ocular manifestations, even after long-term treatment and negative baseline screening. Close multidisciplinary collaboration is essential for the diagnosis and management of ocular TB in this population.

title: Recognizing Odontogenic Maxillary Sinusitis in the ENT Clinic: Four CT Findings That Should Prompt Dental Evaluation.
abstract: Objective: This retrospective cohort study evaluated the proportion of maxillary sinuses with radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution among patients with imaging-confirmed acute or chronic maxillary sinusitis presenting to a single academic ENT clinic over one year. Sixty-five CT scans (84 sinuses) underwent multidisciplinary review for prespecified radiographic features. By highlighting imaging findings indicative of dental origin this study aims to improve recognition of possible odontogenic disease and appropriate multidisciplinary evaluation. Methods: Sixty-five patients were evaluated. Inclusion criteria required a visit diagnosis of chronic maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J32.0) or acute maxillary sinusitis (ICD10 J01.00, J01.01), and a sinus CT within the preceding year. Each scan underwent multidisciplinary review by an oral and maxillofacial radiologist, an otolaryngologist, an otolaryngology resident, and a medical student. Scans were evaluated for maxillary sinus floor mucosal thickening and radiographic features suggestive of an odontogenic contribution, including periapical pathology, oroantral communication, large dental restorations, and widened periodontal ligament (PDL) space. Dental referral recommendations were based on multidisciplinary consensus from CT findings alone. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics. Results: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution were identified in 50/84 (59.52%) affected maxillary sinuses from 40 patients. Among these 50 sinuses, 17 (34%) showed widened PDL space, 15 (30%) showed oroantral communication, 28 (56%) showed periapical pathology, and 9 (18%) showed large dental restorations. There was consensus among the multidisciplinary team that in retrospect, among the 40 patients with OS, 38 required dental referrals. Conclusion: Radiographic findings consistent with an odontogenic contribution indicated a higher single-center cohort prevalence than expected based on population-level prevalence reports. The findings support deliberate review of the maxillary dentition on sinus CT, with this study outlining the key imaging features for odontogenic sinusitis.

title: MTL-LymphNet: A Lightweight Multi-Task Learning Framework for Simultaneous Lymph Node Segmentation and Metastasis Classification in Thyroid Cancer Ultrasound.
abstract: Ultrasound assessment of cervical lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma is crucial but suffers from inter-observer variability. Existing deep learning solutions typically use separate single-task pipelines, resulting in parameter redundancy. We propose MTL-LymphNet, a lightweight, backbone-agnostic multi-task learning framework that simultaneously segments lymph nodes and classifies metastasis within a single forward pass, evaluated across 3 backbones and 4 loss weighting strategies. On 338 images from 2 independent clinical centers, MTL-LymphNet achieved an internal cross-validation Dice coefficient of 0.891 ± 0.022 and AUC of 0.948 ± 0.027. Bidirectional external validation revealed substantial domain shift, with cross-center Dice of 0.865 and 0.779, and AUC of 0.733 and 0.830. The multi-task configuration offered a favorable efficiency-performance trade-off (∆Dice = Δ, -0.014, P < .0001) for 40% fewer parameters than separate models. No backbone or weighting strategy consistently dominated, and calibration degraded substantially under domain shift (ECE: 0.049 internally vs 0.178-0.304 externally), requiring center-specific recalibration before clinical use. To our knowledge, this is the first MTL framework for cervical lymph node analysis with bidirectional multi-center validation and systematic ablation. With a compact size of 22.6 to 29.1 MB and CPU inference of 81 to 131 ms, MTL-LymphNet demonstrates technical feasibility as a CAD tool warranting prospective validation.

title: Cardiac diagnostic modalities in polycythemia vera: A narrative review.
abstract: Polycythemia vera is a chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm in which erythrocytosis, Janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription activation, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and abnormal blood-cell activation converge to increase cardiovascular risk. This narrative review examines how electrocardiography, echocardiography, coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, and right-heart catheterization contribute to recognition and characterization of cardiac involvement in polycythemia vera. Reported abnormalities include QT and P-wave changes, atrial arrhythmias, acute coronary syndromes, subclinical biventricular dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, intracardiac thrombosis, and hypertrophic remodeling. Large observational datasets in myeloproliferative neoplasms also exhibit clinically important burdens of myocardial infarction, heart-failure hospitalization, bleeding, and echocardiographic pulmonary hypertension, although polycythemia vera-specific estimates remain limited. Baseline cardiovascular testing is increasingly relevant before novel therapies and trial enrollment; however, an abnormal test should prompt confirmation, reversible-cause assessment, and protocol-specific review rather than be treated as a universal contraindication. Hematocrit control and low-dose aspirin reduce thrombotic events, while evidence that cytoreductive therapy reverses electrocardiography or imaging abnormalities remains sparse. A symptom- and risk-directed diagnostic approach, integrated with hematology and cardiology assessment, is therefore more defensible than routine universal cardiac screening.

title: An Integrated Approach to MSI-High Colorectal Cancer Therapy in a Young Patient: A Clinical Case.
abstract: BACKGROUND Colorectal cancer (CRC) is extremely rare in adolescents and often presents with advanced disease because of nonspecific symptoms. Deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) and microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) are important biomarkers that influence prognosis, treatment selection, and the need for genetic evaluation. We report the case of an adolescent with MSI-H-associated CRC presenting with acute intestinal obstruction. CASE REPORT A 16-year-old male initially underwent appendectomy for presumed acute appendicitis. Persistent postoperative bowel obstruction prompted computed tomography (CT), revealing a descending colon tumor requiring emergency Hartmann's procedure. Histopathology demonstrated mucinous adenocarcinoma, pT4N0M0, with vascular invasion. Immunohistochemistry showed loss of MSH2/MSH6 expression with retained MLH1/PMS2, indicating dMMR and findings highly suggestive of Lynch syndrome, although germline testing was unavailable. Molecular analysis identified a KRAS mutation without NRAS alterations. Given his multiple high-risk features, including T4 disease, bowel obstruction, vascular invasion, mucinous histology, and very young age, he received 12 cycles of adjuvant FOLFOX chemotherapy. Treatment was well tolerated, and he remains disease-free more than 5 years after completion of therapy. CONCLUSIONS This case highlights the diagnostic complexity of adolescent CRC and the need to consider colorectal malignancy in young patients with persistent or atypical abdominal symptoms. Routine MMR/MSI testing and comprehensive molecular profiling are essential in young-onset CRC to identify patients who may have hereditary cancer syndromes and require genetic counseling. Although limited to a single case, this report underscores the importance of multidisciplinary decision-making and individualized treatment based on clinicopathological and molecular characteristics, which may contribute to favorable long-term outcomes.

title: Artificial intelligence in ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography: a bibliometric analysis.
abstract: Aim To analyze research landscapes, hotspots, and trends in artificial intelligence (AI) applied to ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) from 2015 to 2024, aiming to reveal global collaborations and guide future research. Methods We retrieved publications from Web of Science Core Collection using AI and OCTA-related search terms. After screening, 237 articles were analyzed with CiteSpace (version 6.3.R1) for co-citation, collaboration, and keyword burst analysis. Results Annual publications grew rapidly since 2017. China (94 publications) and the US (86 publications) were the most productive and influential countries. Research focused on: deep learning algorithms and vessel segmentation, ocular disease diagnosis including diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma, and automated vascular quantification and multimodal imaging. Key limitations included small sample sizes and limited algorithm generalizability. Conclusion The integration of AI with OCTA has significantly advanced the automation and precise quantitative analysis of ophthalmic vascular imaging, demonstrating substantial potential for diagnosing various retinal and choroidal diseases. Future efforts should focus on developing more robust and interpretable AI models, conducting large-scale, multi-center clinical validation, and establishing standardized imaging and analysis protocols to ultimately realize the widespread adoption of AI-OCTA technology in routine clinical practice.
originalAbstract:
Aim

To analyze research landscapes, hotspots, and trends in artificial intelligence (AI) applied to ophthalmic optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) from 2015 to 2024, aiming to reveal global collaborations and guide future research.

Methods

We retrieved publications from Web of Science Core Collection using AI and OCTA-related search terms. After screening, 237 articles were analyzed with CiteSpace (version 6.3.R1) for co-citation, collaboration, and keyword burst analysis.

Results

Annual publications grew rapidly since 2017. China (94 publications) and the US (86 publications) were the most productive and influential countries. Research focused on: deep learning algorithms and vessel segmentation, ocular disease diagnosis including diabetic retinopathy and glaucoma, and automated vascular quantification and multimodal imaging. Key limitations included small sample sizes and limited algorithm generalizability.

Conclusion

The integration of AI with OCTA has significantly advanced the automation and precise quantitative analysis of ophthalmic vascular imaging, demonstrating substantial potential for diagnosing various retinal and choroidal diseases. Future efforts should focus on developing more robust and interpretable AI models, conducting large-scale, multi-center clinical validation, and establishing standardized imaging and analysis protocols to ultimately realize the widespread adoption of AI-OCTA technology in routine clinical practice.

title: Deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognostic prediction in locally advanced cervical cancer through 18 F-FDG PET/CT and MRI combination
abstract: Abstract Background Precise pretreatment risk stratification is critical for guiding treatment intensification and personalized follow‑up in patients with locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT). This study developed and validated a deep learning integrated clinical-radiomics model for prognosis prediction in patients with LACC treated with CCRT, using dual-modal pretreatment imaging from 18 F-FDG PET/CT and contrast-enhanced MRI. Methods We retrospectively collected 346 patients (276 for training and 70 for testing) with LACC between June 2016 and October 2021. Radiomics and deep learning signatures were extracted from PET/CT and MRI. These signatures were integrated with the clinicopathological factors into a nomogram for clinical applications. Models were constructed using eleven machine learning algorithms, and a clinical-radiomics-deep learning model (CRDLM) was developed. The evaluation of the model’s performance was conducted through the metrics of the area under the curve (AUC). Results The CRDLM demonstrated superior predictive performance (AUCs of 0.998 (95% CI: 1.00–1.00) for training cohort and 0.901 (95% CI: 0.83–0.97) for testing cohort), which is significantly superior to conventional clinical factors (FIGO stage and SCC-Ag, AUC = 0.605–0.658). In addition, the CRDLM which combined radiomics with deep learning significantly outperformed the radiomics‑only model (AUC = 0.793, p = 0.006). Sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of CRDLM reached 0.947, 0.725, and 0.786, respectively. Conclusions The CRDLM provides robust prediction of disease progression in LACC patients who received CCRT, which may facilitate personalized treatment strategies and improve clinical outcomes. Further validation in multicenter prospective studies is warranted.

title: Can Chest CT Differentiate Between Low-Risk and Higher Risk Congenital Lung Lesions in Infants?
abstract: Abstract Purpose To determine whether chest CT can differentiate low-risk congenital lung lesions (pulmonary sequestration and CPAM type 2) from higher-risk lesions (CPAM type 1 and pleuropulmonary blastoma [PPB]) and thereby support the selection of patients for conservative management. Methods In this retrospective study (2003–2024), we identified infants with congenital lung lesions who underwent chest CT and subsequent pathologic confirmation. Two pediatric radiologists independently reviewed the anonymized CT scans, blinded to clinical and pathologic data. Lesions with a systemic arterial supply or predominant hyperinflation were classified as low risk; those with a solitary cyst, a cyst > 2 cm, or a complex cyst without systemic supply were classified as higher risk. Diagnostic confidence was graded as low, moderate, or high. Pathologic diagnosis served as the reference standard, and Cohen’s kappa was used to assess interobserver agreement. Results Eighty-three children (52 male) were included. Low-risk lesions (n = 73) comprised CPAM type 2 with or without sequestration (n = 51), isolated sequestration (n = 18), and other benign lesions (n = 4). Higher-risk lesions (n = 10) included CPAM type 1 (n = 8) and type I PPB (n = 2). For moderate-to-high-confidence diagnoses, sensitivity was 100% for both radiologists; specificity was 89.2% and 93.1%; and the negative predictive value was 100%. Interobserver agreement was almost perfect (98.4%; κ = 0.95). Conclusion Chest CT enables reliable differentiation of higher-risk from low-risk congenital lung lesions and can guide the selection of candidates for conservative management.

title: Unintentional Weight Loss Preceding Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report and Review of Possible Mechanisms
abstract: Abstract Background Unintentional weight loss is not a recognized presenting feature of multiple sclerosis (MS) and is more commonly associated with malignancy, chronic infection, endocrine disorders, gastrointestinal disease, or systemic inflammatory conditions. We report an unusual case in which marked involuntary weight loss preceded the diagnosis of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). Case Presentation: A 37-year-old man presented with acute gait impairment and right lower-extremity weakness. Retrospective history revealed gradual unintentional weight loss from approximately 97 kg to 68 kg over nearly two years despite preserved appetite and the absence of gastrointestinal, infectious, endocrine, or constitutional symptoms. Extensive investigations, including laboratory testing, infectious screening, tumor markers, upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, abdominal ultrasonography, and chest imaging, failed to identify an alternative cause. Neurological examination demonstrated right lower-extremity weakness, generalized hyperreflexia, bilateral pyramidal signs, and an Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) score of 4.0. Brain and cervical spinal cord magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple typical demyelinating lesions fulfilling the 2017 McDonald criteria for MS. The patient received intravenous methylprednisolone followed by rituximab (1000 mg every 6 months). During four years of follow-up, the EDSS score improved from 4.0 to 1.0, MRI studies remained stable, and body weight gradually returned to two years before the start of the disease. Conclusion This case describes marked, unexplained weight loss preceding the diagnosis of RRMS, which resolved after treatment initiation and disease stabilization. Although causality cannot be established, the temporal association suggests that clinically significant weight loss may represent an uncommon and underrecognized manifestation of active MS. Further studies are needed to clarify the frequency and mechanisms of weight changes in MS.

title: Follicular Dendritic Cell Sarcoma Arising in the Aortopulmonary Window: A Case Report of Complete Resection Using Proximal Pulmonary Artery Control
abstract: Abstract Background: Follicular dendritic cell sarcoma is a rare malignant neoplasm, and its occurrence in the aortopulmonary window is exceptionally uncommon. Tumors in this location are technically challenging because of the limited operative space and their close relationship to the aortic arch, left pulmonary artery, left main bronchus, and left recurrent laryngeal nerve. We report a case of follicular dendritic cell sarcoma arising in the aortopulmonary window that was completely resected using a strategy for proximal pulmonary artery control. Case presentation: A 46-year-old man was referred to our institution after an abnormal mediastinal shadow was incidentally detected on chest radiography. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography showed a 48 × 29 mm well-circumscribed mass in the aortopulmonary window, broadly contacting the aorta, left pulmonary artery, and left main bronchus. Positron emission tomography showed moderate fluorodeoxyglucose uptake without distant metastasis. Endobronchial ultrasound-guided transbronchial needle aspiration suggested a neuroendocrine tumor but did not establish a definitive diagnosis. Surgical resection was performed through median sternotomy combined with a left anterior second intercostal thoracotomy. Because direct exposure and encirclement of the tumor-adjacent left pulmonary artery were considered hazardous, proximal vascular control was established through the transverse pericardial sinus before tumor manipulation. Division of the ligamentum arteriosum increased pulmonary artery mobility and improved exposure of the operative field. The tumor was completely separated from the left pulmonary artery, aorta, left main bronchus, and recurrent laryngeal nerve without combined organ resection. Histopathological examination showed spindle-shaped tumor cells arranged in whorled and rosette-like patterns. Immunohistochemical staining was positive for CD21, CD23, D2-40, and somatostatin receptor 2, confirming follicular dendritic cell sarcoma. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient remained free of recurrence 3 years after surgery. Conclusions: Complete resection of a tumor arising in the aortopulmonary window can be facilitated by secure proximal pulmonary artery control and mobilization of surrounding structures. These technical principles may also be useful for other tumors in this anatomically complex region when direct manipulation of the tumor-adjacent pulmonary artery is considered hazardous.

title: Association of intratumoral and peritumoral apparent diffusion coefficients with stromal tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte levels in primary triple-negative breast cancer: a retrospective 3-T MRI study
abstract: Abstract Background Tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) are associated with treatment response and prognosis in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), but their assessment requires tissue sampling. We investigated whether routine pretreatment imaging findings, particularly intratumoral and peritumoral apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) measurements on 3-T breast MRI, were associated with stromal TIL levels and evaluated an exploratory MRI-based model. Methods This single-center retrospective study included 79 consecutive women with primary TNBC assessed between November 2016 and October 2023. High TIL status was defined as stromal TILs ≥ 10% in pretreatment biopsy specimens. Mammographic, ultrasonographic, MRI, and ¹⁸F-fluorodeoxyglucose PET/CT findings were analyzed when available. A prespecified MRI-based logistic regression model included intratumoral ADC, peritumoral ADC, and MRI margin. Discrimination was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis and internally validated using 1,000 bootstrap resamples. Associations with pathological complete response (pCR) were explored. Results High TIL status was present in 57 of 79 participants (72.2%). Among 76 participants with MRI, higher intratumoral ADC (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 6.96; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.47–19.67; p < 0.001) and lower peritumoral ADC (adjusted OR, 0.27; 95% CI, 0.11–0.66; p = 0.004) were independently associated with high TIL status. The exploratory MRI-based model had an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.934 (95% CI, 0.879–0.989) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.914. Intratumoral ADC alone had an AUC of 0.856 (95% CI, 0.768–0.944). The associations remained consistent after adjustment for the MRI system and in the analysis restricted to the predominant Ingenia 3.0T system. In exploratory analyses, pCR was more frequent in participants with high versus low TIL status (58.1% vs. 7.7%; p = 0.001) and in those with high versus low intratumoral ADC (57.1% vs. 8.3%; p = 0.003). Conclusions Routine intratumoral and peritumoral ADC measurements were associated with high stromal TIL status in this single-center TNBC cohort. The exploratory MRI-based model showed good discrimination after bootstrap correction. External multicenter evaluation is required before clinical use.

title: Edematous dermatomyositis as a rare cause of isolated bilateral arm swelling in a patient with urothelial carcinoma: case report and literature review
abstract: Abstract Background Edematous dermatomyositis (DM) is a rare manifestation of idiopathic inflammatory myopathy and may initially resemble vascular causes of upper-limb swelling. Early recognition is clinically important because severe cases require prompt immunosuppressive treatment and because adult-onset DM, particularly in the presence of anti-transcription intermediary factor 1-gamma (anti-TIF1-γ) antibodies, has a close association with malignancy. Case presentation: An 86-year-old Caucasian woman with recently treated high-grade, muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder presented with a 2.5-week history of progressive, severe bilateral upper-extremity edema, proximal muscle weakness, and a violaceous eruption involving the periorbital region, face, anterior neck, and upper chest, accompanied by Gottron papules. Duplex ultrasonography excluded upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis and superficial venous thrombosis. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the chest and abdomen excluded central venous obstruction, thoracic or abdominal tumor recurrence, and metastasis. Electromyography and bilateral shoulder/upper-arm magnetic resonance imaging were compatible with active myositis, and myositis serology was positive for anti-TIF1-γ antibodies. During hospitalization, muscle weakness and dysphagia progressed rapidly. After insufficient clinical response to prednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin, rituximab was administered as salvage therapy. Despite treatment, weakness and dysphagia progressed, and the patient died 6 weeks after admission. Conclusions Edematous dermatomyositis should be considered in the differential diagnosis of otherwise unexplained bilateral upper-limb edema after upper-extremity venous thrombosis and superior vena cava syndrome have been excluded, particularly in the presence of proximal muscle weakness, dysphagia, or dermatomyositis-specific cutaneous findings. The diagnosis of DM should prompt structured oncologic reassessment and surveillance, especially in patients with anti-TIF1-γ positivity or recent malignancy.

title: Interactive Lesion Segmentation in Whole-Body PET/CT and Longitudinal CT: The autoPET/CT-IV Challenge
abstract: Abstract Deep learning enables automated tumour segmentation in whole-body positron emission tomography and computed tomography, but robustness remains limited by heterogeneous tracer uptake, anatomical variability, and inter-center differences. We report the fourth autoPET challenge, which evaluated interactive lesion segmentation using incremental simulated user prompts and longitudinal lesion segmentation from paired baseline and follow-up scans. In the interactive task (Task 1, ~ 30,000 training and ~ 3,000 test lesions), submitted methods improved with additional user input and achieved a mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.74 at the final interaction step, with performance remaining robust across tracers and centers. Longitudinal segmentation (Task 2, ~ 7,500 training and ~ 4,500 test lesions) was substantially more challenging, with a best mean Dice similarity coefficient of 0.38. Here, we show that interactive segmentation can combine automated inference with iterative expert input while maintaining performance across heterogeneous imaging domains, whereas longitudinal lesion prediction remains limited by temporal and anatomical variability.

title: Halo-Femoral Traction and Staged Surgical Correction for Severe Rigid Adult Scoliosis: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Surgical correction of severe rigid adult spinal deformities (ASD) with Cobb angles exceeding 100° is highly challenging due to risks of neurological injury and poor spinal flexibility. Preoperative halo-femoral traction enhances spinal compliance, facilitating safer staged corrective surgery. Few cases of this procedure for curvatures approaching 150° have been reported. Case Presentation: A 24-year-old female presented with severe right thigh and knee pain secondary to a 148° rigid thoracolumbar kyphoscoliosis. Initial imaging revealed minimal flexibility (bend correction to 94°) without neural compromise. The patient underwent continuous halo-femoral traction for several weeks to improve spinal flexibility, The patient was managed via a sequential two-step protocol: initially, under anesthesia, halo and femoral pins were placed to apply continuous traction for maximizing spinal flexibility. Subsequently, the patient underwent definitive single-stage posterior spinal instrumentation and deformity correction. Intraoperative neuromonitoring was utilized throughout to ensure neurological safety. Continuous multi-modal intraoperative neuromonitoring (IONM), including somatosensory-evoked potentials (SSEPs) and motor-evoked potentials (MEPs), was utilized throughout all two surgical stages. No significant or sustained changes in SSEP or MEP signals were observed during the corrective maneuvers, supporting the early detection of potential neurological compromise and guiding safe deformity correction. Conclusion: Postoperatively, the patient achieved significant correction with a final Cobb angle of approximately 50°, accompanied by marked pain relief, improved truncal balance, and enhanced functional status as measured by clinical video-based clinical observation of gait. Radiographs at 6 weeks and subsequent follow-ups demonstrated stable fusion and sustained alignment. No neurological deficits or major complications were observed. This case illustrates the feasibility of utilizing prolonged halo-femoral traction combined with a carefully planned surgical algorithm in the management of extreme rigid adult scoliosis. The technical and strategic framework provided herein may inform clinical practice guidelines and warrants further investigation in larger cohorts.
